pr_title: Allow to select multiple remote nodes at runtime
pr_body:
Closes #93628.

[Screencast_20241125_111648.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7018978a-ca5f-42c3-b70f-96a4c63a397d)

### Features Implemented

- Multi selection of multiple nodes, even if from different types. The properties shown in the inspector will be the ones shared by all the ones selected, like how `MultiNodeEdit` works.
- Region selection for `Node2D`/`Control` and `Node3D` nodes.
- Additive selection: holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> will add/remove items to the selection group instead of overriding it.

**Sponsored By:** 🐺 Lone Wolf Technology / 🍀 W4 Games.
pr_comments:
I want some feedback on how to handle limiting selection of too many nodes, because that carries the risk of encoding of the data failing and no selection occurring.

- What the default limit should be? 10-ish or so?
- Should it be a hard limit, not allowing to select further nodes? Or a soft one, only printing a warning when the limit is exceeded?

Maybe hard limit with warning?
How many nodes can be selected before it breaks?

@KoBeWi Missed your message, sorry.

It depends on the data size of the objects. On my end for example, selecting more than 30 `Button` nodes starts to break things.

So limit it to 20-25, if someone tries to select more nodes pop a warning toaster. The limit can be configurable in editor settings. Personally I rarely select more than 5 nodes; most often it's to move them in the scene, which is not something you can do in Remote tree.
The selection limit has been implemented.

Having investigated this a bit, I notice that most of the code for `_find_3d_items_at_rect()` is copied from `Node3DEditorViewport::_select_region()`, but adapted to the SceneDebugger. This creates a couple problems:
1. The code to support orthogonal cameras was lost in translation. This PR only works for perspective cameras
2. There are a lot of unnecessary calculations that make the code difficult to read and run much slower than it should
3. The code mixes the camera override with the scene camera at times leading to issues when you switch back to the scene camera after changing the camera override

It needs to be cleaned up before merging.

@clayjohn

1. That was because I couldn't get the perspective selection to work, so I didn't think I would fare any better with orthogonal.
2. Would help if you pointed to specific sections.
3. Could you give me a step-by-step? I'm unable to reproduce this issue on my end.

> 2. Would help if you pointed to specific sections.

- All of `_get_screen_to_space` can be replaced with `camera->project_position`
- `zofs` is never actually used, it just has `znear` added and subtracted to it and gets cancelled out
- The creation of a mesh collider for each mesh and testing against it (removed in my suggested change above)

I can submit another diff to clean up these parts if you want

> 3. Could you give me a step-by-step? I'm unable to reproduce this issue on my end.

Sure, run the game with the scene debugger. Switch to the camera override, then rotate the camera to the side. Then turn off the camera override and try selecting an object.

> Sure, run the game with the scene debugger. Switch to the camera override, then rotate the camera to the side. Then turn off the camera override and try selecting an object.

It still works fine here? At least single selection is, can't test multi selection because it's still broken.

> > Sure, run the game with the scene debugger. Switch to the camera override, then rotate the camera to the side. Then turn off the camera override and try selecting an object.
> 
> It still works fine here? At least single selection is, can't test multi selection because it's still broken.

The problem is only for multi selection. And ya, whenever the override camera is different from the actual camera it is totally broken, which is the problem

After some back and forth with Clay, the multi selection for 3D is complete! 3D selection of physics bodies works a little differently however, as it triggers without encompassing the entire body like in the editor. This can be changed in the future though, so not a blocker.

I think this is finally ready for a review.

issue_context.title: You cannot multi-select and multi-edit in the remote scene view
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

4.2.2.stable

### System information

Godot v4.2.2.stable - Windows 10.0.22631 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.4633) - AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 Threads)

### Issue description

You cannot multi-select and multi-edit in the remote view. It only let's you select a single node at a time. 

I would expect to be able to select multiple nodes of the same type and edit them all in one go like I can in the scene view.

Not sure if this should be logged as a proposal? I would expect it to work, so it felt more like a bug.

### Steps to reproduce

Run a scene with multiple nodes. You cannot Ctrl/Shit select multiple nodes in the remote view.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

NA

review_comments:
This seems to cause a compilation error in `target=template_debug` (which apparently isn't being run as part of CI currently):

```
scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp:428:11: error: 'fieldwise_assign' was not declared in this scope
```

What do you think would be the best course of action here? Wrapping it around `TOOLS_ENABLED` solves it, but that means per field value changing would be broken for remote debugging. So maybe making "math_fieldwise" be available for debugging templates would be the best alternative?

Forgive the potentially dumb question, but can you actually remote debug an exported debug template? I can't say I've ever tried.

If so, then yeah, it doesn't strike me as a particularly heavy or otherwise dangerous function to expose, so I would probably opt for just exposing it for `DEBUG_ENABLED` as well. If you need it you need it.

> Forgive the potentially dumb question, but can you actually remote debug an exported debug template? I can't say I've ever tried.

Yes, it's mostly for mobile debugging.

> If so, then yeah, it doesn't strike me as a particularly heavy or otherwise dangerous function to expose, so I would probably opt for just exposing it for DEBUG_ENABLED as well. If you need it you need it.

Gotcha.

You could instead replace it with editor layout. It's global for editor.
The project metadata are per-project, not very useful for Game tab.
I would actually disagree. Different projects sometimes require different workflows, so making those be kept in a per-project basis makes sense.
